bindings.explanation: REQ-1-3-1 requires the CSV importer to parse data in the original row and column order and to handle commas enclosed in double quotes. SP.parseCSV deletes the field that immediately precedes a quoted field whenever that field is numeric (row.pop()), so for the record 'East,1200,"Open,Open"' the numeric field 1200 is dropped and the quoted field slides from column C into column B. The fixture is a valid CSV row with a numeric text field followed by a quoted field containing a comma - exactly the case the requirement names - and the simpler control row proves the parser works for plain input.

bindings.requirement_text: Users start an import by clicking the "Import CSV" button on the workbook home page. A dialog named "Import CSV" provides a file control labeled "CSV file" and a "Confirm import" button. The system parses data in the original row and column order, preserves empty fields, supports UTF-8 Chinese text, English text, and numeric text, and correctly handles commas enclosed in double quotes, escaped pairs of double quotes, and line breaks within fields; a field that begins with a double quote but has no closing double quote is invalid CSV and must be rejected with "Invalid CSV file format. Import failed." After a successful import, a new workbook is created whose name is the file name with its final .csv extension removed, and Sheet1 opens with the complete CSV rows, columns, and original text; the first row remains ordinary data. After refresh or reopening, grid content and row/column order remain unchanged. If parsing or import fails, no workbook link with that name may appear on the home page, and no partial import result may be displayed or retained.

bindings.explanation: REQ-2-2-2 requires that after columns are inserted the filter still applies to the adjusted region, and REQ-2-2 requires filter views to remain consistent with the moved data. SP.insertCols remaps cells, formula references, validation rules and pivot source ranges, but never remaps sheet.filters[].range. Once the filtered data shifts right, the stored filter range no longer contains the filtered header, SP.hiddenRows can no longer resolve the 'Sales' key and every row becomes visible. The fixture is the startup workbook with only an explicit filter added over its own header row, and the precondition proves the filter hides the right records before the transition.

bindings.requirement_text:
Users insert a blank column to the left or right of a target column, or delete the target column, through the column-header menu in the current active worksheet. The column-header menu provides "Insert 1 column left", "Insert 1 column right", and "Delete column". On insertion, all complete data, validation rules, and formula references in the target column and subsequent columns shift right together; on deletion, subsequent columns shift left and rules on the target column are removed. Data outside the deleted column is preserved; affected formulas display the adjusted original formulas and correct results, while direct references that cannot be preserved display #REF!; filters continue to apply to the adjusted region. If a shifted 0-to-100 numeric validation rule rejects an out-of-range value, the page displays "Please enter a number from 0 to 100". After pivot-table source columns move, existing results remain unchanged until "Refresh pivot table" is clicked, after which the moved fields are used. If a selected header is deleted, refreshing or opening the pivot table editor displays a visible error requiring the field to be reselected and preserves the last successful result. If the operation fails, an error is shown and the grid retains the pre-operation structure immediately and after refresh.

Page reference:
![image](reference/manage-columns.png)

bindings.explanation: REQ-4-1-1 requires aggregate functions to ignore empty cells and COUNT to count only numeric cells. When the argument is a single A1-style reference to an empty cell, SP.cellValue reports the cell as empty but the formula engine converts that reference to numeric 0 before collecting arguments, so '=COUNT(A1)' counts the blank cell and the grid shows 1 instead of 0. The precondition shows the same aggregate correctly counts a numeric cell, so the fixture is a valid worksheet and the difference is not a parsing problem.

bindings.requirement_text:
Users enter formulas beginning with an equals sign through the grid or formula bar in REQ-3-1-1. Formulas must support at least numeric constants, parentheses, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, A1-style references within the same worksheet, and SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MIN, and MAX over contiguous ranges; cross-worksheet references are not required. The grid displays results calculated from the current source data, and when a formula cell is selected the formula bar displays the original expression entered by the user; both persist after refresh. Function names are case-insensitive; aggregate functions ignore empty cells, COUNT counts only numeric cells, and SUM/AVERAGE/MIN/MAX use only numeric cells and do not treat blanks as zero.
Page reference:
![image](reference/basic-formulas.png)

bindings.explanation: REQ-3-2-2 requires undo to restore grid values, row/column structure and rule ranges from before the operation. Validation rules live in ARC.state.ui, outside the workbook snapshot that pushHistory/doUndo store, while SP.insertRows rewrites their ranges in place. Undoing a row insertion therefore restores the cells but leaves the 0-to-100 rule on the shifted range A2:A4, so A1 (which was constrained before the operation) is no longer constrained. The precondition establishes the valid starting state (data in A1:A3 plus the rule covering A1).

bindings.setup: window.ARC = window.ARC || {}; ARC.state = ARC.state || {}; ARC.state.ui = { rules: { 'wb-1/sheet-1': [ { id: 'v1', range: 'A1:A3', type: 'number', min: 0, max: 100 } ] } }; ARC.state.workbooks = [{ id: 'wb-1', name: 'W', lastUpdated: '2024-01-01 00:00', activeSheet: 'sheet-1', worksheets: [{ id: 'sheet-1', name: 'Sheet1', cells: { A1: '1', A2: '2', A3: '3' }, sel: { r: 0, c: 0, r2: 0, c2: 0 }, validations: [], filters: [] }] }]; ARC.route = function () { return { name: 'workbook', params: ['wb-1'] }; }; ARC.save = function () {}; ARC.render = function () {}; ARC.notify = function () {};
bindings.precondition: var wb = ARC.state.workbooks[0]; assert.strictEqual(wb.worksheets[0].cells['A1'], '1'); assert.ok(ruleFor(wb.worksheets[0], 'A1'), 'A1 is constrained by the 0-to-100 rule before the operation');
bindings.check: var wb = ARC.state.workbooks[0]; pushHistory(wb); insertRows(wb.worksheets[0], 0, 1); doUndo(); var after = ARC.state.workbooks[0].worksheets[0]; assert.strictEqual(after.cells['A1'], '1', 'undo restores the grid values'); assert.ok(ruleFor(after, 'A1'), 'undo must also restore the validation rule range so A1 stays constrained');
bindings.requirement_text: Users can undo recent cell edits, bulk pastes, range moves, and row/column structure changes in the current workbook session. The toolbar provides buttons with the accessible names "Undo" and "Redo"; Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y perform the same operations. Undo restores the grid values, original formulas, row/column structure, rule ranges, pivot-result validity, and calculation results from before the operation; consecutive undo operations restore changes in reverse order, and redo reapplies the complete operation that was just undone. Undo in one workbook must not modify another workbook. The state after each undo or redo persists after refresh; the history itself only needs to exist within the current session and may be empty after reopening. If a new modification is made after an undo, the "Redo" button becomes disabled and Ctrl+Y cannot restore the old branch.
